incompetech.description: What makes a Bossa Nova a Bossa Nova? Whatever it is, this has it double! Or maybe it is just compensating for its relatively simple chord progression. Enjoy your Bossa! Probably. Probably a Bossa Nova.

incompetech.title: Lobby Time
incompetech.description: Welcome to the lobby of the FUTURE! Luxurious automatic ashtrays, and modern green vinyl furnishings set off the shag carpeted walls. Enjoy a Rusty Nail from our cheerful bar staff (with a complimentary cheese and fruit plate before 5pm). We feature prime rib dinners every day that ends in a "y"! Remember to tip the bellhops at least 5 cents per bag. Enjoy your stay! This was written 2 years before it was published, because I didn't have a good enough upright bass sample to make it go.

incompetech.title: Salty Ditty
incompetech.description: Avast ye maties! All your boat are belong to us! Super chipper piratey-like 8bit tune. I mean, it could be used for non-nautical things, but the audience will probably be all like "Hey! Why is there an 8-bit pirate shanty going on here!?" Perfectly loopable for all your casual seafaring games. Or game reviews. Or actual voyages. Or voyage reviews.

incompetech.title: Gregorian Chant
incompetech.description: Is it a real Gregorian Chant? Nope. For one - there are no real words in it. Honestly, I don't want a religious exaltation mucking up my fantasy world. So if you're building a historically accurate "Monk Simulator: Year of Our Lord 882!", just move on. The other reason this isn't real is I never learned how to read that notation. There are insufficient sticks for the rhythms in the notation... I know, there is a real convention that you can learn. I just grabbed a few pieces of the sheet music from the 1200s, and guessed at how to do it. Sounds reasonable enough to me! (says the guy who knows virtually nothing about the art)

incompetech.title: Nowhere Land
incompetech.description: Fun fact: Working title was "Arpeggiator Rock From the 80s 1". Fun fact: This piece consist entirely of single notes being passed to a stack 5 different synths at the same time. Each synth has a different program running on it that triggers more notes. Fun fact: Scotland isn't a nation. It is technically an empire that claims sovereignty over Paraguay's 400k sheep and also Neptune's "shepherd" moon Despina.

incompetech.title: Vanishing
incompetech.instruments: Prepared Piano, Bass Clarinet, Cello, Clarinet, English Horn, Tuba, Trombones, French Horns, Oboe, Synth, Violin, Flutes
incompetech.description: Several distinct moods are found in this piece. They start at 0:00, 1:23, 2:31, and 3:10. They do all flow into each other, but can be sliced apart pretty easily. Some are quite beautiful, so stick with this piece. Excellent piece for filmmakers!

incompetech.title: ZigZag
incompetech.description: A little aggressive, a little chill, a little groovy, a little cool. Not entirely appropriate for all occasions, but in the right context - it may be just what you need! This is the "Goth 7th-Grader" of the music world. The instrument with the sharp chord hits is the mighty Mellotron, which is a pre-sampler sort of analog keyboard attached to a bunch of tape players. I cheated. This one is digital.

incompetech.title: Chill Wave
incompetech.description: I was looking for a subject to analogize the depth of my knowledge for the Chill Wave genre of music. Wikipedia was there for me with entire things that I didn't even know were things; Randle Cotgrave! Yeon Namgeon!  Digital Mammographic Imaging! Rebelj, Serbia! In brief... I know nothing about Chill Wave. Hope you enjoy the fruits of ignorance!

incompetech.title: Industrial Cinematic
incompetech.description: The Year: Future Year. The planet has been ravaged by desertification... that apparently no one saw coming... Not sure how that happened, I mean Jeez! Anyone ever hear of a little disaster called "The Aral Sea"? That seriously screwed up... like... everything. I guess the dam is supposed to help, but I'm seriously not holding my breath. Oh. Industrial-sounding music.

incompetech.title: Airship Serenity
incompetech.description: This is the first slow 8-bit piece I ever tried. There was some skepticism going in, but holy man! This turned out great! You can use it for your game credits, or more chill parts of your game. Maybe at the Healing Shack, or the Abe Vigoda Memorial Pagoda and Koi Pond. The uncompressed download has a bonus  percussion track.

incompetech.title: Bit Shift
incompetech.description: This is about as exciting/happy as simple 8-bit exciting/happy music gets. It's Swingin'! It's Singin'! It's using a whole lotta apostrophes! Sometime's incorrectly! Anyhoo, take a listen to this one. Ye shan't be dis'appointed! Bleep, bloop... bloop, bleep.

incompetech.title: Magic Forest
incompetech.description: Remember that time you were lost in the woods and you were visited by the clan of  centaurs, and they were super suspicious of you, but decided to take you back to their settlement anyway? It never happened! That was a screen memory! There are no centaurs, and they wouldn't live in forest settlements! That was an alien abduction. The aliens planted the memory of the forest centaurs so your brain wouldn't implode with the knowledge of trans-dimensional beings... such as themselves. And... unrelated, but... what comes to mind when you think about the smell of wet cardboard and Sriracha?

incompetech.title: Dreamer
incompetech.description: Gorgeous, rich piano chords run counter to subtle percussions. This piece is a workhouse for video productions. Don't bother with the preview, just download this thing. Because seriously... planning a cat rescue? This will work. Attending someone else's family reunion and trying to convince them you're related? Yes. This will work. Time lapse of a rocket assembly? Obviously. I'm looking at you, ESA!

incompetech.title: Nonstop
incompetech.description: From what I can tell, this piece has no genre... it is an odd mix of a few things, but not enough of any one of them to be considered a member of that group. So, when you find a new critter which is certainly a new species... likely a new genus... probably a new family... and seriously might be a order. It has an exoskeleton, gives birth to live young (asexually somehow?), has a beak... We recognize all those parts, but it doesn't fit anything. Might be a new phylum.

incompetech.title: Soaring
incompetech.description: While not an epic hour-long relaxation juggernaut, Soaring is an excellent relaxation workhorse with just enough mystical qualities to keep it from being truly peaceful.  Imagine a calm monkey hanging out at a remote monastery who, from time to time, will touch a tree - causing the tree to age a decade in a matter of seconds. I mean... still pretty calm, but something isn't right about that.

incompetech.title: District Four
incompetech.description: Deep grooving crazy big percussion. Super danceable! High energy, without every getting the way. Useful for tech videos, badass characters, or general listenings! The download comes with all the parts separated out as well as a bonus track at 165 beats per minute (slightly slower and even deeper grooving!).

incompetech.title: Rocket Power
incompetech.description: Funky drum machines? Yes, please! Also a killer bass line. This is both big and fun... kind of like the Paul Bunyan Experience... if Paul Bunyan were hip. Unlike most of my tunes, this one has an actual ending! Uncompressed download comes with all the parts to make your own mixes - should this one be insufficient.

incompetech.title: Secret of Tiki Island
incompetech.instruments: Bass, Piano, Percussion, Vibraphone, Guitar, Vocals, Organ
incompetech.description: Co-written with Bryan Teoh while he was on vacation (Thanks Bryan!) this is all the mystery and chill groove you need. So come on you cats and swingers, enjoy yourself a Jet Pilot (served in a pineapple of course) and help unravel the Secret of Tiki Island! Can you save yourself and the island from the Volcano!? No. Of course you can't. It is a freaking VOLCANO. If the pyroclastic flows and lahars don't kill you, the carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide probably will. Uncompressed download comes with 10 different stems so you can mix your own!

incompetech.title: Super Power Cool Dude
incompetech.description: This piece was built almost entirely with arpeggiators. What does that mean for you? Probably nothing. But holy man! Does this sound like it is from 1983! So, pop a tape of "Flashdance" in your VCR... and then spend like 8 minutes rewinding it... because, apparently your cousin couldn't be bothered to do that. Seriously, Sally! You did the same thing when I lent you "Smokey and the Bandit II", and I didn't say anything because you had a hard week, but still managed to make the Jell-o Salad with the grapes for the family reunion... which was nice. Anyway, I'll probably just get you one of those $20 tape rewinders they have at Radio Shack for your birthday. I also enrolled you in the Battery of the Month Club. You're welcome.

incompetech.title: Giant Wyrm
incompetech.description: Oh! The horror! This is NOT a fun piece. It WILL make you feel like there is something seriously wrong. Did those veins on my forearm always look like that? I mean, they're doing a weird criss-cross pattern... and they look REALLY blue. I would have noticed that before, surely! I wonder if this has anything to do with the  meteor that came down in Mr. Wilson's pond last night? Uncompressed download comes with 4 stem files in case you don't need all the creepy, all the time.

incompetech.title: Master Disorder
incompetech.description: Sometimes you do things with little expectation of how it is going to finally turn out. Maybe you're making a hummus and cauliflower pizza roll... Will it work? Who knows! You can sort of make the hummus taste like Italian hummus if you use enough oregano, basil, and... chili flakes or something. So, then you make it, and realize it should be called a "Flaccid Spiced Hummus Ball". Eating a flaccid spiced hummus ball helps to assess your life choices... that eventually led you to eating a flaccid spiced hummus ball.  Uncompressed download comes in 4 speeds; 72, 80 (this one), 88, and 96 beats per minute. Flaccid spiced hummus ball.

incompetech.title: Deadly Roulette
incompetech.instruments: Drums, Bass, Synth Bass, Guitar, Vibraphone, Percussion
incompetech.description: Jazzy! Gumshoe-y! Mystery-y! I suck at making adjectives. Who needs adjectives anyway! I'm fine without adjectives. How fine without adjectives, you may ask? I can't say - as that would require some sort of descriptor! And I don't need descriptors in my writings... Maybe one... tiny little... NO! What am I thinking!? I refuse! I've completely had it with adjectives! Hah! Adverbs work perfectly fine! Woohoo! Adverbs! And before I get mail... adjectives killed my family, so I can go off on them all I want.

incompetech.title: Basic Implosion
incompetech.description: Upbeat, bright, and super catchy! Just try not to rap to this piece! TRY IT! You can't, can you! I mean... I can, but I've been training to not rap my entire life. It started with me not-rapping in my childhood in the upper midwest. My lack-of-rapping hit a new high while on a high school band trip to Disneyworld, and was again bolstered in a crazy non-rap filled Spring Break in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario. There's just something about not-rapping and industrial forestry...

incompetech.title: Eternity
incompetech.instruments: Guitar, Bass, Drums, Electric Piano, Synths
incompetech.description: This is like... the ultimate in high-class non-offensive music. You can have this going at the hippest highest-class hotel in the world, and it'll feel at home. You can also put in less-classy places to make them feel classier! Like the opium den you built in your garage, or that tiny closet at your office where lunch-room recyclables go to get sticky and smell bad. I mean seriously... I don't think they ALL started out sticky.

incompetech.title: Hidden Past
incompetech.description: Pipes, pipes, and more pipes! Irish? Scottish? Celtic? I have no idea. But sure - could be any of those. Let's call it "Ancient British Isles".

incompetech.title: Chillin Hard
incompetech.description: Cross Hip-hop with Shoegaze and what do you get? That was not a joke. That was the description of this piece. If you have a show that opens with a shoegaze band, and then headlines a hip-hop group you could use this as the clever bridge between them! Also, you should immediately fire the concert manager. That was a terrible idea.

incompetech.title: Lewis and Dekalb
incompetech.description: Southern trap influenced rap pile of musical forklift platypus... okay, I don't know what these words mean. But if you understood them - we're all good. You know what you're getting, and... that's all I can hope for really. Truth in advertising!

incompetech.title: Vicious
incompetech.description: Bit of swing in your rap? Sure! Why not! I like swing... but NOT TOO MUCH! Just here and there... you know, to alleviate the monotony. Sort of like that one teacher you had in Social Studies that unexpectedly did something cool - like play a game - but only twice a year... and they were both in the first month, so all you ended up with was 8 months of continual disappointment. Screw you, Mr. Meuller! I still don't care about checks and balances!

incompetech.title: Fife and Drum
incompetech.description: Welcome to Historic Williamsburg! Nestled between "That's-OK Greenpoint" and "Still-Kinda-Frightening-In-Many-Areas Bushwick", Historic Williamsburg offers you a link to the past that you'll love! Trucker hats, coffee shops, mustache wax, artisanal mac+cheese, used book stores - come experience part of America's Past! And when you're done; "Get the 'L out of Williamsburg!" [ *L may not be running. ]

incompetech.title: Killers
incompetech.instruments: Guitar, Choir, Percussion, Basses, Cellos, Violas, Violins
incompetech.description: This piece starts BIG. Originally, this piece started slowly and built... and then I got bored and chopped out all the slowness. There are still dynamics, but if you need bigness from the get-go - here's what you get! Vroom! BIG BIG BIG! Could be too big. Could be. Probably isn't.

incompetech.title: Carpe Diem
incompetech.instruments: Clarinet, Ukulele, Flute, Guitar, Xylophone, Percussion, Bass
incompetech.description: Yeah Boyzzz! BGM Music in the HOUSE!!!! In this case, "BGM Music" means "Background Music... Music". You want royalty-free!? You got it! You want ukulele mastery!? You got that, too! You want a piece that's a GNDN piece!? DONE! It's like a whole new genre of undistinguished music! It is sort of bouncy, and cheery. So... somewhat distinguished. It is really hard to hype this piece, but it is wicked-useful!

incompetech.title: Inspired
incompetech.description: Quite a broad piece. Could be used for corporate films of intricate industrial processes, or a flashback scene to the time at the lake a few summers ago. Maybe good background to your cousin's magic show at the last family reunion. Or a film where you do "industrial processes" at the "lake" with your "cousin". It is really quite versatile!

incompetech.title: Furious Freak
incompetech.description: Starts thin and explodes suddenly and massively around the 44-second mark. The uncompressed download also comes with a cut where it starts out big. I'm assuming it will be used for the outro parts of videos.

incompetech.title: Professor Umlaut
incompetech.description: This piece started its life as a random challenge on a show I do on Twitch.tv called "The Wheels of Doom!". The 4 randomized elements that came together here were: Drum Machine, Strings, Xylophone, and Comedic. I think it worked out pretty well!

incompetech.title: Thief in the Night
incompetech.description: Laid-back, grooving, and cool. Did I mention cool? You need a cool piece. That is a statement you NEED a cool piece. Lucky for you, this IS a cool piece. Super clean production will allow this piece to fit into most things. I'd personally use this piece for a super badass character.

incompetech.title: Floating Cities
incompetech.description: It is the future? It certainly sounds like it... What would I use this for? Probably a video game with non-action gameplay. Certainly a montage of some futuristic film... or maybe one of those sandwiched scenes where a person is walking in the rain, but you don't get any of the sounds of the actual rain... just this piece. No dialog, no voiceover, just walking. Do they have a name for those scenes? They must.

incompetech.title: Thunderbird
incompetech.description: Wikipedia describes the Thunderbird as "a supernatural bird of power and strength". It will also ask you to disambiguate it from the automobile made by Ford from 1955 to 2005. I'm sure it was a nice car. I've never owned one. But there were a lot of them! The late 70's Thunderbirds are particularly horrifying... They had those headlight covers that flipped up... because that was a good idea at some point. But this piece! Oh! This piece! Atmosphere like you wouldn't believe! The flute is just so earthy! The organic drones are also beautiful. The whole thing is beautiful. Kind of like you went to an alien day spa in another dimension where days last for years, but you still never get all wrinkly when you're in the bubbly warm waters. mmmm... bubbly warm waters... with the slight possibility of a serial killer.

incompetech.title: Rynos Theme
incompetech.instruments: Violins, Violas, Cellos, Basses, Flutes, French Horns, Trombones, Tuba, Percussion, Piano
incompetech.description: Starts small, gets big... then smaller, then REALLY big... then small again. Kind of like a turtle. Actually, it is entirely possible that I just kept seeing different turtles. I mean, they all sort of look like turtles; I wasn't tagging them or marking them with chalk or anything. Chalk will probably just wash off in the pond anyway. Oh! Kind of like a puffer fish! Like a musical puffer fish! Perfect.

incompetech.title: Slow Jam
incompetech.description: Well, this is interesting... Smooth sine bass contrasted with a lovely excited drum machine and then... the magic! Genre bending magic! You're a cool kid right? This is for you. You're welcome. Think 'trap' meets 'R&B' meets 'shoegaze' meets some other genre that is SO COOL there isn't even a name for it yet. Download comes with a not-quite-so-slow version that is not quite so slow.

incompetech.title: Curse of the Scarab
incompetech.instruments: Xylophone, English Horn, Oboe, Bass Clarinet, Flutes, French Horn, Basses, Cellos, Percussion
incompetech.description: Five! Five full minutes of battle fighting action bits with a bit of an Egyptian flair! For some reason I associate English horn with desert nomads. There must have been some cultural reference in my youth to that effect. Super crazy awesome brass is super crazy awesome... wait for it... you'll be glad you did! Uncompressed download comes with fully loopable mix.

incompetech.title: Crypto
incompetech.description: Very moody little piece with some melodic interest. Tension could be high grade or low grade depending on your context. Waiting for a drug deal to go through in Belize? This'll work. Concerned about the health of your hyacinth macaw while waiting at the vet office? This'll work. Waiting for the OSHA all-clear at your box factory? This'll work. It is mainly about waiting for things. Probably not good things.

incompetech.title: Casa Bossa Nova
incompetech.instruments: Piano, Flute, Bass, Percussion, Organ, Guitar, Mellotron
incompetech.description: Okay, the tuning on the bass is a bit off here and there, but the heart is in the right place.Throw a filter on this and use it an your waiting area jam. Or on-hold music. Or pre-show music for your militia function. I'm sure the calming aspects would be very welcome in all the situations! Oh, you can also use this in your dance routines. Because bossa novas rock! ... or they Bossa... not sure.

incompetech.title: Blue Ska
incompetech.instruments: Drums, Bass, Guitar, Organ, Trumpet, Trombone, Tenor Sax
incompetech.description: Run of the mill ska!? No such thing! Well, this is as close to that reality as you can get. It is high energy, dance-inducing, happy fun times for everyone who was born after... like... the Industrial Revolution... So, there may be some trees and fungi that don't find this fun; but, I can't really care about their concepts of fun too much. I assume they don't like winters, but they just all sort of stand around all the time.

incompetech.title: Immersed
incompetech.description: Minimal and somewhat droney in parts, this has a beautiful calmness about it. You can use it to sell anti-depressants or high performance automobile parts. Also useful for time-lapse photography of the night sky... or maybe a rocket launch.

incompetech.title: Overworld
incompetech.description: You want adventure? You want a princess? You're not getting the princess, buddy... but Adventure Awaits in "Overworld"! How much adventure? A statistically significant amount. Somewhere in the neighborhood of 18ppm... (or roughly 18 milligrams per liter... the density of adventure is unusually high, and in some cases even at 18ppm you will get a weight closer to 19mg/L.) Download comes with a faster version, a SUPER faster version, and a slower version without percussion for lazy title screens and whatnot.

incompetech.title: Cyborg Ninja
incompetech.description: Your girlfriend has be kidnapped by ninja! Stage 1: Desert. Avoid the flaming balls and shoot cyborg ninja in the eye to win round. Retro-gaming circa 1988. I was seriously considering naming this piece "Flaming Balls" as that would also have been appropriate. Cyborg ninjas are just a little more '1988' to me. Need 10 hours of this? Loop it!

incompetech.title: Myst on the Moor
incompetech.description: Could be the thinking music for a quiz show about the paranormal? "Where does the Sasquatch typically vacation... is it A, The High Mountains... B, Unexplored Cave Systems...  C, Graceland... or D, In another dimension - similar to, but not strongly coupled with our own reality. Take your time and answer whenever you're ready.... A, B, C, or D... Would you like to consult the Tarot or do an entrail reading?" I love the flute bits in this piece.

incompetech.title: Happy Happy Game Show
incompetech.description: Okay, it is a 12 bar blues, but you got to stick around at least until the horns! I couldn't start with the horns as that would be a frightening level of happy. The uncompressed download also comes with a perfectly loopable track for those who don't want the party to end.

incompetech.title: Cuban Sandwich
incompetech.description: A groovy little piece excellent for an evening at your local cabana.

incompetech.title: Corruption
incompetech.instruments: Basses, Cellos, War Horn, Brass, Percussion, Choir
incompetech.description: Formerly titled "Tyranid Battle Loop", this piece was written for down and dirty... and very very long battle scenes for space bug critters. But you can use it for anything you like! Got a video where you stuck a cucumber on a drone to terrorize your cat? Boom! Corruption. Or those really gross films of people removing cysts? ug. don't use this for that. Actually, why are you posting that? Don't do it. Just... ug. can't unsee...

incompetech.title: Clash Defiant
incompetech.instruments: Basses, Cellos, War Horn, Brass, Percussion, Choir
incompetech.description: You want battle music? You can't HANDLE the battle music! Meh. You probably can. As battle music goes, this is pretty tame - no blaring trumpets or hyperactive xylophones... Why? Dialog! You can actually talk over this battle music! Feel free to punctuate with your own stabs after you cut around your dialog. Or don't. You can use this as a loop on your Twitch stream for anything... battle-y. That rough spiccato bass line is off the hook! (Do people still say "off the hook"? I might be a few years late on that.)  .

incompetech.title: Heavy Heart
incompetech.description: We've all been there. It is a little sad, a little hopeful... like when you finally set your rescue owl back into the world. You're sad to see her go, but you hope for the best. You've done all you can inside... her wings work pretty well now, and she can snatch the mice from your living room floor even when you put in a bunch of fake plants in the way to give the prey cover. Nothing to do now but hope Blossom can rule the night as you hoped she one day would. Also... time to buy a bunch of mousetraps.

incompetech.title: Voice Over Under
incompetech.description: This is a piece of music classified as "GNDN". Goes Nowhere. Does Nothing. It sort of sits there and just repeats mild variants. There isn't even an ending.  Yet, this was all on purpose. This piece was designed for keeping energy in news reports or review segments where there is a lot of talking. There is no end so it is easy to loop to any length. There will come a time in your editing career where you will need this piece. Best to download it now.

incompetech.title: Final Battle of the Dark Wizards
incompetech.filename: Final Battle of the Dark Wizards.mp3
incompetech.instruments: Synths, Choir, Percussion, French Horns, Trumpets, Violas
incompetech.description: Slowly building tension power that really gets going when the super gnarly drums kick in after the violas... sort of in the section with the trumpet.... then there's this part that's all like "AHHHH AHHHHHH AAAAAHHHHHHHHH!!!!" And then there's some more "AHHHHHHHHH" and then even more and its like a new key or something, and the drums are all distorted and slammin', and then there's this wwwwwwhhhhHHHHHOOOOOOOSHHHH!!!! and some more french horn majesty - and like another keychange or something... but definitely some bass drum. The big bass drum that you stand up and hit with a mallet... not the kind you stick on the floor... and stomp on a pedal that is attached to a mallet that hits the floor drum.

incompetech.title: Fresh Air
incompetech.description: This was a quick improvisation that turned out pretty listenable! Original title was "Sofa King Beautiful", but I figured "Fresh Air" worked better. Since this is a piece for solo keyboard, I included four alternate keyboards in the uncompressed download. They all have subtly different feels. Electric Piano, Grand Piano, Spinet Piano (out of tune), and a piano where you tap the strings rather than hit it with the hammers.

incompetech.title: OctoBlues
incompetech.description: Just yer basic 12-bar blues. Guitar courtesy Brett Van Donsel.

incompetech.title: Mighty Like Us
incompetech.description: Only 6 monophonic synths and a drum set in this entire, extremely peppy, undeniably enthusiastic, off-kilter, oddly satisfying electronic piece! Even at that, it gets pretty dense near the end.   Try this one! You'll like it! (you'll probably like it... figure about 90 percent guaranteed to like this piece by the end.) The uncompressed download comes with a mix done using electronic drums. It has a very different and more machine-like feel. Chances you'll like that one are lower... but it is totally usable for a harsher feel.

incompetech.title: Garden Music
incompetech.description: This epic 41-minute relaxing juggernaut is a continually changing yet always pleasant piece. How pleasant? Very, very pleasant. You can just put this one on and drift away to the imagined utopian land of your choosing! Suitable for day-spa background music, dental office calming music, very long form landscape or train videos, governmental intake and processing videos. The uncompressed download does not contain separate files, just the one big 650 meg wav file.

incompetech.title: Christmas Rap
incompetech.description: I was commissioned to do some music for the play "Twas The Night Before Christmas" by Ken Ludwig. The mp3 download here is the main holiday-themed rap from near the end of the play. The uncompressed download comes with that as well as the Girl/Mouse rap from earlier in the play - which you can hear on Soundcloud as "La Souris". The full download also has the exciting fanfare intros to the holiday rap.

incompetech.title: Baba Yaga
incompetech.description: A little smooth, a little edgy, this has some wicked percussion in it. I forget how many drums there are in this - but it is quite a lot. Doesn't overpower, though. This one could also be considered 140 beats per minute, depending on how you count. It is right in that grey area. And no, I don't know what the words mean... I'm not even certain of the language, or if it is a language. The uncompressed download comes with an extra No Vocals Mix.

incompetech.title: Suave Standpipe
incompetech.instruments: Bass, Accordion, Drums, Electric Piano, Guitar, Horns, Organ, Synth, Sax, Vibraphone
incompetech.description: You know what's cool? A standpipe in the winter. I imagine this one with a hip mustache and a plaid beret. Enough of the imagery, this is a little downtempo chill piece with lush horn punctuation. Suitable for: walks in the rain, time-lapse videos, sad cooking shows.

incompetech.title: Leopard Print Elevator
incompetech.description: Smooth. Seriously smooth. Smooth like you can't even imagine how smooth this is. Still has a lot of life, though! The uncompressed download comes with an alternate mix with a super deep electric bass for even more smoothness! Did I mention it is smooth? Sort of like an early 1970's era vibe to it. But smoother.

incompetech.title: Pixelland
incompetech.description: What do you get when you cross some 8-bit music technology with Dixieland music? Well... you get stuff that sounds like this. The uncompressed download comes with a pile of extra stuff, like versions at 220, 230, 240, and a whopping 275 beats per minute! That's really fast. It also has loops that don't go through the modulation so you can repeat them as long as you'd like!

incompetech.title: Relaxing Piano Music
incompetech.description: You can only title a piece Relaxing Piano Music once in your life, so you better bring it! Piano? You bet! Relaxing? Indeed! Music? Close enough! This 24-minute epic of calm is great for that chilly winter day, or lazy summer day... All the seasons! Wherever you need calm, you can get it here! Peaceful exclamation points? Yes!! All of them! De-stressing while studying for an exam? Go for this one! Doing a retrospective on the life and times of your pet chinchilla? You're welcome! All the calm! ALL THE TIME!!! Key of G. You can make your own mixes with the uncompressed downloads to only include the melodies you want if you like!

incompetech.title: Fretless
incompetech.instruments: Guitar, Ukulele, Drums, Bass, Glockenspiel, Music Box
incompetech.description: Nice, forward-pulling piece pretty much guaranteed to offend no one. This piece is a little more complex than others in this genre because of the multiple countermelodies. They clear out many times, and make room before coming back in. You can make your own mixes with the uncompressed downloads to only include the melodies you want if you like!

incompetech.title: Bit Quest
incompetech.description: Wonderful 8-Bit ditty for an exploring action adventure platformer. My favorite part is at 16 seconds in... The rest of the piece was written around that theme. Check it out, yo! Careful of the spiked kittens on level 7... not cuddly.

incompetech.title: Groundwork
incompetech.description: Stop it! Stop complaining, it is supposed to end like that! This is a loopable piece. Why? You never know how long your voice-overed tour of the cardboard factory is going to take... Or your real estate tour... Or your appendectomy video... Or your video of that one train by your house. Uncompressed download comes with a faster version, and a slower version.

incompetech.title: Kings of Tara
incompetech.instruments: Bass, Drums, Drum Kit, Guitar, Flute, Banjo
incompetech.description: This one is just cool. If you just tried to dance to this and fell over, that's because every measure is missing one beat. Still it grooves quite well, assuming you can groove in 7/4 time. Uncompressed download comes with individual tracks so you can make your own mixes.

incompetech.title: Welcome to HorrorLand
incompetech.description: Welcome to HorrorLand! Please keep all arms, legs, and eyestalks inside the vehicle at all times. All exits are clearly marked. There are no exits. Do not attempt to leave HorrorLand. This will end badly for everyone. Please note: it will end badly if you do not attempt to leave as well. So, it is really up to you. Feel free to split up your group and explore. That is always a great idea!

incompetech.title: Ultra Polka
incompetech.description: I tried to do an EDM piece using one of my new accordions... turns out, accordion just doesn't have the fast attack needed to do fast electronic things. The melody and chords were written for a diatonic button box, but I was never able to get the live recording to work. No worries! I just turned this monster up to 11. The uncompressed download comes with a faster and slower version.

incompetech.title: The Show Must Be Go
incompetech.instruments: Bass, Guitar, Diddley Bow, Clarinet, Trumpet, Vibraphone, Horns, Drum Kit, Percussion
incompetech.description: Sort of inspired by the 1930s, and sort of inspired by all-out weird. Definitely recommend taking a listen to this piece. Make sure you get to the 1 minute mark... fun times trumpet playing await! I personally enjoy how the clarinet play tries to follow the trumpet player - doesn't work out so well.

incompetech.title: What Is Love
incompetech.description: What is love? Apparently, it is an odd mix of 1980's synthy love songs and modern trap beats. I don't think there is anything like this out there... which may be a fine thing - or I've just invented a genre. Crooner-Synth Trap-Pop.

incompetech.title: The Lift
incompetech.description: A little trance-y and a dance-y, this piece takes a while to develop (like most EDM things these days). The full width of the piece is realized around 1:40. Not so much a drop and a gentle trip down a hill, really - but still satisfying! That note at the end? Surprisingly difficult to do that... I know you're thinking - Hey! That just sounds like noise! Well, yes and no. But it is worth it!

incompetech.title: Danger Storm
incompetech.description: So this one sounds like what is sounds like. The high quality download has a few bonus mixes. The Tin Mix is excellent for small speakers. The Phased Mix is like... sort of groovy, man. The 90 mix is a bit faster. And the House Mix is super dance party fun times!

incompetech.title: Crowd Hammer
incompetech.instruments: Guitar, Percussion, Diddley Bow, Flute, Oboe
incompetech.description: Originally written as an establishing shot for a psychological thriller. This has a very earthy/folky feel about it. Little slow, little edgy... I don't know. Take a listen. I mean, I'll keep trying to describe this but, I'm not doing too well here. There's this flute thing... uhh... Slightly creepy movie score? Yet oddly comforting? Sure. Let's go with that.

incompetech.title: Upbeat Forever
incompetech.description: Ska! Ska! Ska! At least, I hope it gives that impression. Works pretty well for a lively background to most anything! This was written for an improv comedy group... so they would have something reasonable to sing to - if an audience member suggests it.

incompetech.title: Intrepid
incompetech.instruments: Basses, Cellos, Tuba, Trombones, Prepared Piano, Voice, Drums
incompetech.description: This has a little bit of early music flair to it with a nice vocal performance (if you don't like the vocals, you can get a version without in the super download). I've listened to this piece non-stop for like an hour. Still beautiful! The least you could do is listen to this once! It is only a few minutes. Go ahead!

incompetech.title: Spellbound
incompetech.description: Reverbs, reverbs, reverbs! You want reverbs in you music, you got reverbs right here! Room reverbs, plate reverbs, even some spring reverbs! It is amazing! It is incredible! How can there be so much reverb?! So... why... You get a very hollow spooky thin feeling with the reverbs. This started out as an attempt to understand Witch House music. Pretty sure I still don't understand it.

incompetech.title: Mystic Force
incompetech.description: Vaguely exotic sounding, yet still comfortably tonal, this piece certainly falls between some cracks. Gamelan is listed as an instrument... but that's sort of like listing an orchestra as an instrument... which I sometimes do. The other thing in here is that helicon. Imagine you take a french horn (which is like 5 meters of tubes) and make it even bigger! I guess it is also the name of a mountain in Greece? I did not use the mountain in this piece.

incompetech.title: Kawai Kitsune
incompetech.description: A very electronic semi-soothing piece of bleeps and bloops! I originally wrote this piece to be calm, but in the uncompressed download, there are a couple of faster versions! YOU CANNOT CONTAIN THE EXCITEMENT!

incompetech.title: Spy Glass
incompetech.instruments: Piano, Bass, Drums, Vibraphone, Saxes, Trumpet, Flute
incompetech.description: The year is... I have no idea. Timeless. Could be now, could be in the 1950s. Super cool jazz for your hardcore detectives! Also useful for beat poets! Also useful for ennui or boredom! Well, interesting sorts of boredom.

incompetech.title: Meanwhile in Bavaria
incompetech.description: Technically, it isn't a polka - though you can certainly dance to it. This recording is perfect for all your Octoberfest needs!

incompetech.title: Blip Stream
incompetech.description: You love this, and you know it! It is a little bit simple and a lot bit complicated. Inspired by the days of the video games and early computer music.

incompetech.title: This House
incompetech.instruments: Violins, Violas, Cellos, Basses, Piano, Harp, Celesta, French Horn, Waterphone
incompetech.description: Delightfully creepy, this piece is really difficult to listen to without squirming a bit. I blame the violins... as we all should. Perfect for any scene where something just ain't right!

incompetech.title: Funky Chunk
incompetech.instruments: Bass, Electric Piano, Drums, Guitar, Synth, Horns
incompetech.description: Get down with the 'get down'! A very clean sort of funk thing. Appropriate for a widevariety of exciting sorts of things, including funky dance parties, car washing (dance parties), barbecuing (dance parties), and colonoscopy (dance parties).

incompetech.title: Quirky Dog
incompetech.description: Smooth and jazzy ditty with a fun edge for all your light humor needs! Okay, many of your light humor needs. Excellent for montage sequences dealing with bureaucracy.

incompetech.title: Wagon Wheel - Electronic
incompetech.description: Super jaunty quick tune with 3 distinct parts. The main theme starts in the beginning, Super syncopated theme starts at about a minute in, and the industrial comedy theme starts at 1:30 or so.

incompetech.title: Wagon Wheel
incompetech.description: Super jaunty quick tune with 3 distinct parts. The main theme starts in the beginning, Super syncopated theme starts at about a minute in, and the industrial comedy theme starts at 1:30 or so.

incompetech.title: Lively Lumpsucker
incompetech.description: Hijinks, antics, shenanigan, tomfoolery! We got it all here for you! Solo out of tune piano for all of your slapstick needs! Sheet music available (More button).

incompetech.title: Ossuary 7 - Resolve
incompetech.description: Well, we've come to some sort of ending here... Our relaxation journey is complete, but to be honest, I've had more relaxing times clinging to the single floating piece of flotsam that resurfaced after the ship exploded.

incompetech.title: Ossuary 6 - Air
incompetech.description: Well, something has taken a turn for the not-quite-as-good-as-I'd-like. Slow-moving drone of impending doom!

incompetech.title: Ossuary 5 - Rest
incompetech.description: After some amount of introspection, I can only conclude that this is the afterlife, or some entryway to the afterlife... or a really cool club in the Meatpacking district after-hours. This is the most genuinely relaxing piece of the Ossuary suite... still has a bit of an edge.

incompetech.title: Ossuary 4 - Animate
incompetech.description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary".  Part 4: Animate It is coming for us!!!! ARGH!!!!! RUN! But where!?? Doesn't matter! Try running at the walls!!! No good! They're solid!! Is it still coming!? ARGH! Yup! There it is!!!! Now where!? The ladder!? NO GOOD COMES FROM CLIMBING A LADDER! You should know that by now! It'll just break halfway up OR something will grab your ankle OR BOTH! Just save yourself! There's no good us both getting eaten by that thing!!! Oh! And when you fill out the survey - this holiday was "VERY DISAPPOINTING!"

incompetech.title: Ossuary 3 - Words
incompetech.description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary".  Part 3: Words Odd metals and percussion underscore the only piece in the series with a clear clean synth. There's some amount of technology under this thing. The synth is quickly overtaken by the bizarre drones. Perfect for; being stranded in space... in a ship.

incompetech.title: Ossuary 2 - Turn
incompetech.description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary".  Part 2: Turn More aggressive than part one, something is most certainly going down here. Perfect for; seeing how far down the rabbit hole goes, Loch Ness expeditions, videos about giant capacitors, dinner parties where you want everyone uncomfortable. Gets quite awful around the 3:15 mark. Awful in a good way.

incompetech.title: Ossuary 1 - A Beginning
incompetech.description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary". This piece is a slow-moving edgy drone with an ethereal melody on top. Since this is sort of a new genre, I'm not exactly sure where it is appropriate. Maybe a vampire spa? Dinner music for a psychopath? You'll figure it out!

incompetech.title: In Your Arms
incompetech.description: A piece of music from a more elegant time, 1940. This is a beautiful slow piece that will make you want to pick up some champagne and go off slow dancing with people... or penguins. I like penguins. And now some searchable words: Big Band. 1940s. Forties. Formal Party. Penguin Slow Dance. No Whammies.

incompetech.title: Disco Medusae
incompetech.description: Discomedusae is an obsolesced class of jellyfish. I'm guessing there was some biology schism back in the day and some crazy jellyfish specialist wrote some sort of definitive work on the animals and everyone had to change their classification. The jerk. I mean, it was probably JUST FINE the way it was! But NOOooo! You had to come along and screw up my perfectly good taxonomy key - rendering it USELESS! Hey jellyfish specialist - guess what? No one cares that much anyway! We're all just placating you until you die, and then everyone is going back to using the old keys, which we could at least figure out! This is a disco tune.

incompetech.title: Rhinoceros
incompetech.description: Semi-8 bit, sort of 1980's synth pop crazy thing! Super energy; Crazy fun. Perfect for: automobile reviews, actions montages, martial arts clips, or anything with fast edits that needs a good pace!

incompetech.title: Pyro Flow
incompetech.description: You got flow? You want this. Borderline chill and aggressive, this piece is your man! It does stand alone, but if you got words... it is amazing! Try it! What style is this? I'm not sure. It borrows from a lot - but I don't think it fits anything out there. Rickenbacker bass, gnarled piano, and a distorted drum kit all fit together beautifully. Percussion breakdown at 2:17.

incompetech.title: Phantom from Space
incompetech.description: I need to be careful about naming these things. Could be neo-retro sci-fi - could be straight up paranormal! Whatever it is, there is a major mystery to be had here! Ideal for technology-induced mummy reanimation films. The alternate mixes in the full download both give a slightly different feel - one with no percussion, and one without the theremin-like synth lead.

incompetech.title: Unwritten Return
incompetech.description: Dreamy and edgy; Not a combination you often find, and yet - here it is. The ambiguous and slippery nature of the piece are a wonderful thing. Perfect for scoring a character where the audience is unsure of them. Could be good? Could be evil? WE DON'T KNOW!

incompetech.title: Disquiet
incompetech.description: On January 31st, 2015, I recorded this piece. For some reason, I hit the record button and played. This is all of the notes. There are no other takes; No other files from that day. I don't remember what I was doing, but I was apparently dealing with fear and hope and apprehension... at least that is what it sounds like to me today - months later. Every now and again, I'll find these files - they are something of an emotional journal. Hope you enjoy it as much as I do! Download has the original MIDI file!

incompetech.title: Universal
incompetech.description: Floating and grounding, this piece has a lot of bass guts but still a lot of reach on the high end. Perfect for retrospectives, automobile time lapses, drunken frat parties (black and white), and studying montages.

incompetech.title: Nano Hoedown
incompetech.description: When circuits throw a party, I imagine it sounds something like this. They can be a bit hyperactive at times. The super download comes with a more calm version at 120 beats per minute, and a crazy fast version at 180 beats per minute! All three versions loop perfectly, so you can make this as long as you need it!

incompetech.title: Motherlode
incompetech.instruments: Guitars, Bass, Drums, French Horn, Trumpet
incompetech.description: Big broad sound certain to give a sense of rockin' wonder! It switches back and forth between  faster guitar-driven sections and majestic horn sections. I know - it sounds like it won't work, but it totally DOES work. Just imagine motocross highlights to this! Or any extreme sport that would benefit from the use of slow motion.

incompetech.title: Lost Time
incompetech.description: Is someone dying onscreen, but you still need some dialog so you can't go up against a solo oboe (the universal musical shorthand for death scenes)? We got this! Dark and moving, this piece will make you cry and not get in the way of those final bits of dialog! Also useful for sullen montage sequences of clergy activities.

incompetech.title: Bumba Crossing
incompetech.description: Sparse and beautiful, this piece has a major change in tone at 2:27, moving to a more energetic feel without destroying what came before. Voluminous choirs support the piece at various moments. They also let the drums stand on their own.

incompetech.title: Jellyfish in Space
incompetech.instruments: Guitar, Ocarina, Electric Piano, Bass, Synths, Percussion
incompetech.description: This is somewhat relaxing, while still having some forward momentum. Kind of like sleeping on a train... or taking MBA classes. I like the spinney-sounding synths. The chorus effects give this piece a watery feel. Kind of like a shimmering pond... or being on hold for an insurance company run by sperm whales.

incompetech.title: Exit the Premises
incompetech.description: Big drums start with piece to reveal that they were not establishing the downbeat. Tight synth percussion and 8-bit inspired synths make this piece downright danceable! And who doesn't like a giant 80s synth? Or a 90s chip tunes synth? Or a modern synth? We gots them all!

incompetech.title: Carnivale Intrigue
incompetech.description: Is it a samba? Probably. It also depends on how broadly you define a samba. Percussion comes in heavy later in the piece with a pile of street drummers for a thicker feel. I'm having a hard time describing the exact groove of this piece. "Slightly whiter than average samba"?

incompetech.title: Dreams Become Real
incompetech.description: Beautiful dreamy piece that confuses times and spaces. You really just need to take a moment and listen to this one - because it is really cool. How cool? You should probably find out! There are a lot of extra synth things going on in it that are hidden in and amongst the piano, like one of those hidden picture books with 45 paperclips, but you can only ever see 7 of them.

incompetech.title: EDM Detection Mode
incompetech.description: This is a sort of electronic music with a heavy backbeat and thumpin' bass. There is a significant change in theme at around 2 minutes - so if the beginning is a bit boring, you can start there. There is another fun change at around 3:30. If you didn't like the previous bits, just start there! I think you get the picture.

incompetech.title: Daily Beetle
incompetech.instruments: Ukulele, Guitar, Marimba, Music Box, Toy Piano, Drums
incompetech.description: We have ways of making you happy! This is one of them. Super catchy mid-tempo grooving ukulele-driven happy music. Useful for: feel-good stories, sentimental retrospectives, Minecraft montages, shark attacks, coming of age stories, cooking shows, and baby raves.

incompetech.title: Infinite Perspective
incompetech.instruments: Synths, Voices, Piano, Harp, English Horn, French Horn, Flute
incompetech.description: All the beauty, awe and calm majesty you can handle... without a permit or prescription medication. The download comes with a faster and slower bonus tempo as well as the original sketch on marimba that was used in making this piece!

incompetech.title: Level Up
incompetech.description: Too cool for school! This is a warm and refreshing, yet invigorating piece of 8-bit-like wonderfulness. Lots of modern blipping and bleeping once it gets going. I imagine this piece can be used in a lot of computer games about computer games. There's also a bunch of overdrive on "Level Up". Loops perfectly for all you video game devs out there!

incompetech.title: Hep Cats
incompetech.instruments: Organ, Bass, Percussion, Flute, Electric Piano, Guitar
incompetech.description: Going to the grocery store? Need a theme for that? Maybe you've got a swank cocktail party that needs some swank music? All of these things are possible and more with this upbeat organ-based piece!

incompetech.title: Drankin Song
incompetech.instruments: Violin, Bass, Guitar, Diddley Bow, Drums
incompetech.description: You know those country sing-talking songs? This works GREAT for that. You can also use it for normal country songs. Anything where you need to express yourself about your truck, or losing your girl, or how awesome your mama was... Limitless possibilities! Also works fine by itself.

incompetech.title: Reformat
incompetech.description: Sort of 8-bit retro video glitch. Excellent for a lightswitch rave! This piece loops perfectly. The uncompressed download comes in 140bpm and a super-hyped up 170bpm mix!

incompetech.title: Maccary Bay
incompetech.description: Modern sort of reggae with a lots of layers! Features the wah-riffic guitar work of Mr. Brett VanDonsel.

incompetech.title: Severe Tire Damage
incompetech.description: Ultra-cool downtempo piece with faster driving percussions. Want to look cool? Make this your theme song. Play it loud enough and you can use it for pro-wrestling entrance music! Uncompressed download comes with a bonus 96bpm set.

incompetech.title: Ultralounge
incompetech.instruments: Piano, Bass, Synths, Percussion, Drums, Congas
incompetech.description: You hip? You really hip? Oh, yeah you are! This piece comes from the coolest hippest parts of solar system... from a 1960s pad on the moon. Oh yeah. Dig it, man... dig it. The uncompressed download also comes with an even more chill mix.

incompetech.title: Mary Celeste
incompetech.instruments: Tuba, Bass Clarinet, French Horns, Contrabassoon, Bass Flute, Flutes, Clarinets, Oboe, Marimba, Tubular Bells, Cellos, Violins, Violas
incompetech.description: Dark and broody, this one starts thin, gets really muddy, and then releases to a faster clearer section. Where would I use this? No idea. I'm sure you'll think of something, though!

incompetech.title: Marty Gots a Plan
incompetech.instruments: Cello, Viola, Violin, English Horn, Alto Flute, Percussion, Marimba
incompetech.description: Sneaking around the house? Use this! Planning a comedic caper? Also good! Semi-random pizzicato is like magic for cheeky hijinks. You know... when Marty gots a plan, it aint usually a good one.

incompetech.title: Meatball Parade
incompetech.description: Fast paced, funny, and downright delightful! If you haven't heard this.... seriously take a listen. I'm a big fan of this piece. I get a lot of requests for things like "Yakity Sax", but there isn't really a way to do that without just ripping the piece off. Hopefully, this is enough fun!

incompetech.title: Secrets of the Schoolyard

incompetech.title: Destiny Day
incompetech.description: My work has been seminal in the development of 'structuredly-non-linear symmetrical-music', a highly intellectual, and rather repetitive genre. My newest piece studies, experiences and isomorphically dominates a variety of structured tension-hemiolas. In short, the method must never present the sound-world. I never examine continuities, despite the fact that any gesture or non-linearity can be, and has been interpreted as a rather orchestrally-monophonic set of 'canon-aerophones'. In my most recent work, vibrations, materials and rhythmic oscillations are all used within chaotically-transdisciplinary gestures, allowing the audience to improvise a variety of symbolic idioms. I am very much influenced by the idea of dismissing popular solos, particularly whilst combined with a highly polyrhythmic approach to spaces.

incompetech.description: There are 70s bits, 80s bits, 90s bits.... all soft of mashed up in a salad-mash-soup-like thing.  Super crisp dance mix.

incompetech.title: Gypsy Shoegazer No Voices
incompetech.description: No, I don't know what this is. Same as Gypsy Shoegazer, but without the vocal parts... in case you want to add you own vocal parts.

incompetech.title: Gypsy Shoegazer
incompetech.description: No, I don't know what this is. Some sort of Bulgarian dirge? It has a good 2-part folk melody that is pretty easy to sing, and a wonderful B section with super cadences at the middle and end.

incompetech.title: Hall of the Mountain King
incompetech.description: Edvard Grieg's famous piece from Peer Gynt (1876). You know this piece.  Starts quiet - ends loud. This is a "cinematic mix" that is a little sharper than most recordings and less dynamic. Source recordings placed into the Public Domain by the MusOpen project.

incompetech.title: Bass Walker
incompetech.description: Just your average work-a-day upright walking bass line. Add reverb to taste. Noir!

incompetech.title: Egmont Overture Finale
incompetech.description: Written by Beethoven. The original source recordings for this come from MusOpen (and are available for free!). This mix is slightly augmented, and highly produced in a cinematic style.

incompetech.title: Egmont Overture
incompetech.feel: Dark, Epic, Intense, Mysterious, Somber, Uplifting
incompetech.description: Written by Beethoven. The original source recordings for this come from MusOpen (and are available for free!). This mix is slightly augmented, and highly produced in a cinematic style.

incompetech.title: Reunited
incompetech.description: Super-sappy well-executed little theme. Really opens up at 38 seconds.

incompetech.title: 8bit Dungeon Boss
incompetech.description: A sort of square swing piece using very simple synths (but highly post-processed). It just makes you want to explore that dungeon, doesn't it!? 8bit Dungeon Level is similar but slower.

incompetech.title: 8bit Dungeon Level
incompetech.description: A sort of square swing piece using very simple synths (but highly post-processed). It just makes you want to explore that dungeon, doesn't it!? 8bit Dungeon Boss is similar but faster.

incompetech.title: Video Dungeon Boss
incompetech.description: This a simple "fake bit" composition. I used very simple oscillators for everything, and then processed it quite a bit. Made for a dungeon level for an old-school video game. Loopable. Video Dungeon Crawl is similar but slower.

incompetech.title: Video Dungeon Crawl
incompetech.description: This a simple "fake bit" composition. I used very simple oscillators for everything, and then processed it quite a bit. Made for a dungeon level for an old-school video game. Loopable. Video Dungeon Boss is similar but faster.

incompetech.title: Thunder Dreams
incompetech.description: This is more of a chordal soundscape than a drone. There is a little bit of hope here and there, but it is tempered with a deep sadness. Probably useful after a loss. Beautiful, horrible.

incompetech.title: Static Motion
incompetech.description: Sharp subtle percussive clicks accompany with otherworldly drone.

incompetech.title: Ice Demon
incompetech.description: Hollow creepy background pad. This is not the feel-good hit of the summer. It is more like the cheese-grater to the brain of uncomfortableness.

incompetech.title: Controlled Chaos - no percussion
incompetech.description: Dark background drone made with the new SkannerXT synth. It is a new kind of synthesis that I'm just getting into. Kinda freaky.

incompetech.title: Controlled Chaos
incompetech.feel: Dark, Eerie, Intense, Mysterious, Suspenseful, Unnerving
incompetech.description: Weird synth drone with a soundtrack-style percussion backing driver.

incompetech.title: Blobby Samba
incompetech.description: Super odd fast-and-loose samba-like concoction with wibbly wobbly bits for extra added fun times.

incompetech.title: Satiate - only percussion
incompetech.description: Highly effected percussion piece at a mid tempo. This track was extracted from a larger work, but will lend some motion and reserved immediacy to any scene.

incompetech.title: Satiate - only strings
incompetech.description: I piece unlike anything I've done, this is a very difficult piece to process emotionally. It just never lets the audience rest. There are a lot of uses for this sort of piece.  It is also available with percussion, which gives it a more immediacy.

incompetech.title: Satiate
incompetech.description: I piece unlike anything I've done, this is a very difficult piece to process emotionally. It just never lets the audience rest. There are a lot of uses for this sort of piece.  It is also available with just the percussion, and just the strings... both of which are quite different from the combined.

incompetech.title: Groove Grove
incompetech.description: Background music for ethereal storytelling. It maintains interest, without driving and usurping attention away from the story or visuals.

incompetech.title: Minima
incompetech.instruments: Trumpets, Trombones, Horns, Clarinet, Flute, Oboe, Bassoon, Contrabassoon, Bass Clarinet, Contrabass Clarinet, Percussion, Celesta, Cellos, Basses, Violins, Choir, Timpani
incompetech.description:
The orchestra is woodwind-heavy, it is actually low-winds-heavy so You've got a lot of Contrabass Clarinet,  Bass Clarinet, Contra Bassoon, Bassoon... And they're just pulsing... Pulsing and pulsing and pulsing.
 So what do you use this for? I don't know. Some things that aren't quite real. It's not a very real-sounding thing.

incompetech.title: Steel Rods
incompetech.description: Smashing on a dumpster while pulling off some imitative counterpoint. Is it a fugue? Nah.

incompetech.title: Future Gladiator
incompetech.feel: Aggressive, Dark, Driving, Epic, Mysterious, Unnerving
incompetech.description: Might be soundtrack, might be unclassifiable... pieces like this, I just can't ever tell. Nothing tricksy going on here - just forward motion.

incompetech.title: Summon the Rawk
incompetech.description: Double kick drums, aggressive bass... perfect for: entrance music for pro-wrestlers, annoying the neighbors, playing "air drums", long walks on the beach.

incompetech.title: Evening Melodrama
incompetech.instruments: French Horn, Trombones, Trumpet, Triangle, Violins, Cellos, Basses, Timpani, Snare, Flute, Clarinet
incompetech.description: Theme for a 1980's-esque prime time TV melodrama.

incompetech.title: Healing
incompetech.description: Mostly pentatonic piece. Listening may cause healing of undisclosed issues.

incompetech.title: Brittle Rille
incompetech.description: Quirky rhythms. Raw production.

incompetech.title: Dub Eastern
incompetech.instruments: Bass, Drum Kit, Piano, Guitar, Synth
incompetech.description: Some sort of freakish fusion. No, I don't know what the heck that synth is supposed to be emulating.

incompetech.title: Dub Feral
incompetech.instruments: Bass, Drum Kit, Piano, Guitar, Synth
incompetech.description: Moog-tastic swooping synth played through a crappy guitar amp over the top of a mid-tempo dub groove.

incompetech.title: Drone in D
incompetech.description: A very long piece of highly relaxing music - done as mostly a piano impromptu over a simple drone (very long note). The piece is in the key of D... mostly. (usually, there is an F sharp and C sharp - this uses an F sharp and B flat... there is no name for this that I know of)

incompetech.title: Stormfront
incompetech.description: Intense and reserved, this unrelenting piece of drumming will be well at home in the soundtrack of your summer blockbuster. Super long for splicing.

incompetech.title: RetroFuture Nasty
incompetech.description: One of three mixes of this bouncy rock-funk piece. Same notes. Same instruments... just different mixes.

incompetech.title: RetroFuture Dirty
incompetech.description: One of three mixes of this bouncy rock-funk piece. Same notes. Same instruments... just different mixes.

incompetech.title: RetroFuture Clean
incompetech.description: One of three mixes of this bouncy rock-funk piece. Same notes. Same instruments... just different mixes.

incompetech.title: Music for Funeral Home - Part 11
incompetech.description: This piece works very well for an actual funeral home setting, or any solemn event. The organ is light and flutey, the chords are often meandering, but have some closure now and then. There are 11 parts in this series - totaling about 34 minutes.

incompetech.title: Danse Morialta
incompetech.description: Simple, simple, effective piano piece. This one is hard to pin down emotionally, so I marked it at both somber and uplifting. It is really quite good... though not quite Satie.

incompetech.title: Unanswered Questions
incompetech.description: The solid beat and dark melody reverberate, giving the simplicity of this single-instrument piece the feeling of mounting tension and unease. Useful for a documentary showing pain, poverty, or imprisonment.

incompetech.title: Simplex
incompetech.description: Thin, dark, moody piece that accelerates to the end. Remarkably metered and free at the same time. Guitar is all half muted.

incompetech.title: Music to Delight
incompetech.instruments: Whistle, Bass, Guitar, Wood Blocks, Tambourine, Clapping
incompetech.description: Oh, unclassifiable... this almost makes a mockery of other unclassifiable things. The woodblock player is solid. The tambourine player... not so much. Tin whistle player is delightful!

incompetech.title: Beachfront Celebration
incompetech.instruments: Bass, Percussion, Brass, Steel Drums, Piano
incompetech.description: If you don't get it from the title, I can't help you. The bass player is pretty awesome. Sort of island-y... in a hyper-real way.

incompetech.title: Junkyard Tribe
incompetech.description: Accelerating piece of contemporary electronic percussions. There's some bit crusting going down, and a few other things. No melodies - just the hits.

incompetech.title: Club Diver
incompetech.feel: Aggressive, Dark, Driving, Grooving, Intense, Unnerving
incompetech.description: Almost like euro club meets industrial vampires. I don't think I've ever done anything similar to this from the percussion side... or with those diving chord things.

incompetech.title: Bet You Can ver 2
incompetech.description: Making a musical mockery using the melody from schoolyard taunts. This pieces rawks out. Nigh inhuman drumming in this. This is the faster of a set of 2 pieces with the same content.

incompetech.title: Bet You Can
incompetech.description: Making a musical mockery using the melody from schoolyard taunts. This pieces rawks out. Major props to the drummer. This is the slower of a set of 2 pieces with the same content.

incompetech.title: Peaceful Desolation
incompetech.instruments: Brass, Timpani, Glockenspiel, Flute, Clarinet, Oboe, Strings
incompetech.description: Low-key mood establisher with chords moving in parallel blocks for the melody. Starts dark, ends open and airy.

incompetech.title: On the Shore
incompetech.description: Beautiful, thoughtful piece worthy of character reflection.

incompetech.title: Latin Industries
incompetech.description: Halting electronic dance piece that ends with a giant lush finale.

incompetech.title: Loping Sting
incompetech.description: Just a quick little fun hit.

incompetech.title: Pump
incompetech.description: Longer version of the fast-paced rockin' tune from the fictional band Glory Nugget. Oh yeah, it is bad, and that's what makes it great.

incompetech.title: Iron Bacon
incompetech.description: Mid-tempo rockin' tune from the fictional band Glory Nugget. Can they play? Absolutely not. It is awesome? Absolutely.

incompetech.title: Theme for Harold (var. 3)
incompetech.description: Simple simple 8-bit theme. This is the fastest "Boss Level" version of the three. It was originally written by a puppet, so mostly black keys, which are easier for a puppet to play.

incompetech.title: Theme for Harold (var. 2)
incompetech.description: Simple simple 8-bit theme. This is the mid-tempo version of the three. It was originally written by a puppet, so mostly black keys, which are easier for a puppet to play.

incompetech.title: Theme for Harold (var. 1)
incompetech.description: Simple simple 8-bit theme. This is the laziest and slowest of the three. It was originally written by a puppet, so mostly black keys, which are easier for a puppet to play.

incompetech.title: Light Thought var 2
incompetech.description: This is the faster of a pair of pieces. Useful for non-obtrusive backgrounds to ads or film sequences with voice-overs. No surprises.

incompetech.title: Light Thought var 1
incompetech.description: This is the slower of a pair of pieces. Useful for non-obtrusive backgrounds to ads or film sequences with voice-overs. No surprises.

incompetech.title: Got Funk
incompetech.instruments: Bass, Drum Kit, Piano, Horns, Percussion
incompetech.description: For the gentleman rhymer; funk with a bigger beat and aged effects on piano and horns.

incompetech.title: Promises to Keep
incompetech.description: Slow impromptu for solo piano. A little hopeful, a little sorrowful... I'm sure there is a word for this feeling, but I don't know it.

incompetech.title: Batty McFaddin
incompetech.description: Gimme a C; a bouncy C! Fun, quirky, off key off colour piece with a few different feels in the middle.

incompetech.title: Overcast
incompetech.instruments: Bass, Drum Kit, Synth, Guitar, Piano, Percussion
incompetech.description: A dreamy, watery disco beat with a kick and snare that are slightly outside of classic disco. It seems like this might clear the dance floor at 3am.

incompetech.title: Organic Grunge
incompetech.description: A sort of funky, rocking, semi-swinging piece with enough dirt to make it cool. Like... jeans that were previously worn by coal miners that are sold in high-end stores.

incompetech.title: Wood and Metal and Water
incompetech.description: A slow moving organic ambiance.

incompetech.title: The Whip (Extended Version)
incompetech.description: The extended version of the show theme written for The Whip Podcast.  Aggressive, hip, theme.  Slow fade out at the end.  This version can be looped easier than the shorter version.

incompetech.title: No Frills Cumbia
incompetech.instruments: Drum Kit, Bass, Acoustic Guitar, Piano, Organ, Flute
incompetech.description: A fast cumbia.

incompetech.title: Angels We Have Heard on High
B-Roll
incompetech.description: Good drums, bass, and very good guitar technique.

incompetech.title: Jingle Bells
incompetech.description: Happy, clappy arrangement worthy of a 6th grade band program.

incompetech.title: Noble Race
incompetech.description: Full orchestra plus piano. This is a long piece with several dynamic changes. Semi-heroic at times.

incompetech.title: Prelude and Action
incompetech.description: Building piece that sets up some sweet, sweet action.

incompetech.title: Deep Haze
incompetech.description: A lighter piece than the descriptors would imply. It is more hollow than dark, more motion-forward than driving. Builds continuously but slowly.

incompetech.title: Oppressive Gloom
incompetech.feel: Dark, Eerie, Epic, Mysterious, Somber, Suspenseful
incompetech.description: Moody moody dark score. Almost a death march. Loops pretty darned well - but you need to trim the end.

incompetech.title: Crusade
incompetech.description: Written as travelling music for a video game... this is probably a bit too active for that. There is a beautiful choral section in the trombones at 2:18. Good anvils.

incompetech.title: Brightly Fancy
incompetech.description: A lively little 2-step with interesting chords.

incompetech.title: Hit the Streets v2
incompetech.description: Scoring essentials. You know that one piece of music that you hear when you follow your character out onto the street, and watch them do... something around the neighborhood. That's this. This is the faster version.

incompetech.title: Hit the Streets
incompetech.description: Scoring essentials. You know that one piece of music that you hear when you follow your character out onto the street, and watch them do... something around the neighborhood. That's this. v2 is the same as this but faster.

incompetech.title: Hero Down
incompetech.instruments: Strings, French Horn, Trombones, Percussion, Flute
incompetech.description:
A piece in three or four parts... depending on how you count parts. The penultimate section features a lonely flute, slowly joined by a children's choir, and finally exploding into a giant choral and orchestral ending.

 From the original soundtrack to "The Last Stand of the Mechanolith".

incompetech.title: Mechanolith
incompetech.description: Superlatives abound in this giant orchestral/industrial piece. To be played loud. From the original soundtrack to "The Last Stand of the Mechanolith".

incompetech.title: Unlight
incompetech.feel: Aggressive, Dark, Eerie, Epic, Intense, Unnerving
incompetech.instruments: Basses, Cellos, Violins, Trombone, French Horn, Trumpets, Flutes, Clarinets, Percussion
incompetech.description: This piece is actively painful. It is ugly and nasty and dirty - about as much as you can be using exactly one orchestra. Seriously, there are occasional bits where there are notes - but mostly, it is just... uhh...

incompetech.title: Mirage
incompetech.description: A sort of drone-based piece with something that sounds like a waterphone, and some other things that I don't know what they could be. Super chill - good amounts of tension with some glorious consonants.

incompetech.title: Death of Kings
incompetech.instruments: French Horns, Trombones, Cimbasso, Trumpets, Drum, Chimes
incompetech.description: Deep and rich piece of remembrance for brass. The melody is carried by the horn, with some help later by trumpets.

incompetech.title: Five Armies
incompetech.feel: Action, Aggressive, Dark, Driving, Epic, Intense
incompetech.instruments: Cellos, French Horns, Trombones, Violins, Marimba, Trumpets, Percussion, Oboes, Clarinets, Flutes, Basses
incompetech.description: Big giant building piece starting in 6/4 alternating to 4/4 and back. Soaring ending with a lot of brass.

incompetech.title: The Path of the Goblin King v2
incompetech.filename: The Path of the Goblin King v2.mp3
incompetech.instruments: Strings, Flute, Clarinet, Oboe, Celesta, Timpani
incompetech.description: Slightly faster version of the other similarly named piece, this one has an extra sense of urgency, but still retains the mystery and wonder bits.

incompetech.title: The Path of the Goblin King
incompetech.filename: The Path of the Goblin King.mp3
incompetech.instruments: Strings, Flute, Clarinet, Oboe, Celesta, Timpani
incompetech.description: This is sort of "Spooky Light". It is dark yet playful in a sense. Good for fairy tales or light tension building. It has several small arcs in it - but loops back to the begging.

incompetech.title: The Snow Queen
incompetech.instruments: Strings, Bassoon, Bass Clarinet, Flute, Celesta, Timpani
incompetech.description: Sort of exciting and sort of spooky in that fairy tale sort of way. This is one of my favorite pieces of late. Good interplay of instruments. You can listen to this one over and over. Handy, because it does loop back to the beginning. Major build starting at 1:50 or so.

incompetech.title: Over Under
incompetech.description: Solo bass. Non-consistant tempos. No looping, just playing.

incompetech.title: Bicycle
incompetech.description: Solo bass. No, it doesn't sound like that song. There are only so many ways make a looped bassline sound. This is one of them. Ends in a super build of chords.

incompetech.title: Wet Riffs
incompetech.description: Solo bass with a looping pedal. Very very slow. Super nice. Starts with the highs, and builds interest in the bass.

incompetech.title: Suvaco do Cristo
incompetech.description: Named for a region in Rio, this Brazilian-style carnival piece has a deep dark thickness to it.

incompetech.title: Leblon
incompetech.description: Mid-up-tempo Brazilian carnival style piece. ABA form.

incompetech.title: Lagoa v2
incompetech.description: Brazilian carnival style music at an aggressive tempo. It is not possible to be unhappy listening to this.

incompetech.title: Lagoa v1
incompetech.description: Brazilian carnival style samba music. This is the most chill of the pieces I've made in this style.

incompetech.title: Cool Vibes
incompetech.description: A simple little slow trio for use in such things that require a slow jazz trio. Modulates at the midpoint.

incompetech.title: First Call
incompetech.description: AKA "Warning Call". Three trumpeter version of the 1804 military bugle call. I couldn't get the ensemble to do triple tonguing on the arpeggios. Oh well. Still does the job. Get ready!

incompetech.title: Taps v2
incompetech.description: Solo trumpet version of the 1862 military ceremonial piece.

incompetech.title: Avec Soin
incompetech.description: Super easy-going slow piano piece. Ends quiet and rich.

incompetech.title: Calmant
incompetech.description: Slow moving, semi-arpeggio theme.

incompetech.title: Facile
incompetech.description: Slow, deliberate piano solo - ending on a very satisfying Tierce de Picardie.

incompetech.title: Pensif
incompetech.description: Slow moving cluster chords. Beautiful, I say!

incompetech.title: Our Story Begins
incompetech.description: Interesting 3/4 feel with an accelerando near the end. 5-note groupings pass from the winds to the strings for a while, and the winds come back at the end in a nifty way.

incompetech.title: Chipper Doodle v2
incompetech.description: Happy little tune with asynchronous edits, and unexpected modulations.

incompetech.title: Chipper Doodle
incompetech.description: Happy little tune with asynchronous edits, and unexpected modulations.

incompetech.title: Chee Zee Caves V2
incompetech.description: Loping dissonant loopable atmospheric. Same as Chee Vee Caves, but without the brass.

incompetech.title: Cut and Dry
incompetech.description: Modern-style production of a dance/world music fusion. Laser sharp super compressed mix.

incompetech.title: Cut and Run
incompetech.description: Modern club music.

incompetech.title: Constance
incompetech.feel: Action, Dark, Epic, Intense, Mysterious, Suspenseful
incompetech.description: A low-level intensity burn to underscore a tense situation of some sort. Actually, this will make any scene tense - like it or not.

incompetech.title: Gathering Darkness
incompetech.description: Screeching dark, electronically chattery. Nightmarish.

incompetech.title: Heroic Age
incompetech.instruments: Flutes, Clarinets, Oboes, Trombones, Tuba, Cellos, Basses, Percussion, Celesta
incompetech.description: See title, instrumentation, tempo, and feels for description. Originally written for a live performance.

incompetech.title: Invariance
incompetech.description: One file that contains the same piece in 2 tempos; slower and faster. The slower version gives a more tribal feel - the fast one destroys that, and lends a slight edge-of-the-seat feel.

incompetech.title: The Pyre
incompetech.description: Vaguely medieval overtones. The opening section repeats in the second half with violins added.

incompetech.title: The Cannery
incompetech.description: A giant rousing mechanized heavy piano and heavy percussion piece, mildly reminiscent of Gershiwn or Scott - in 2 small sections.

incompetech.title: Cipher
incompetech.description: I've been told this is R&B, but could be a few other things. It is certainly pretty neat. Warning: Very sticky hook.

incompetech.title: Wallpaper
incompetech.description: Very very clean mix that is non-offensive on almost all fronts. Good spectral distribution - nice lows and highs. 2 catchy synth lines sort of fight for attention, leaving you to ignore them both after a while.

incompetech.title: Presenterator
incompetech.description: 90s vintage presentation music with a bit more production value than the buy-out music of the day.

incompetech.title: I Feel You
incompetech.description: A sort of backgroundy 1980's-ish dreamy rock fusion thingee.

incompetech.title: Bassa Island Game Loop
incompetech.description: Small section of a piece - loopable for all you looped music needs.

incompetech.title: Funk Game Loop
incompetech.description: Looping section of a backgroundy piece of music. It says it is a game loop, but you can loop it for anything you like.

incompetech.title: Slow Ska Game Loop
incompetech.description: Two very different synths bracket the highs and lows of this piece. Loopable for things that require looping.

incompetech.title: Wah Game Loop
incompetech.description: Just a simple funk/rock piece for looping anonymously in the background of things. Organ seems a bit nasal. hmm...

incompetech.title: Quasi Motion
incompetech.description: I don't know what genre this is. Sort of Latin? Broadly? So, if you're looking for something unlike anything else... this may be it.

incompetech.title: Slow Heat
incompetech.description: Very simple polyrhythms and polymelodies.

incompetech.title: Dubakupado
incompetech.description: Named for the sound of the final cadence. This is a nice solid grooving piece - light on polyrhythm -  for 8 percussionists.

incompetech.title: Pixel Peeker Polka - faster
incompetech.description: 8-bit-sounding electronic polka.

incompetech.title: Pixel Peeker Polka - slower
incompetech.description: 8-bit sounding electronic polka.  8-bit-sounding electronic polka.

incompetech.title: Arcane
incompetech.description: Nicely motive tribal/modern percussive fusion.
